uncited: This method extracts a triangulated mesh from an implicit surface by growing a front from a seed point, creating new triangles attached to front edges.

It differs from its parent [Region-growing and Advancing Front](17871-region-growing-and-advancing-front.md) by explicitly handling front self-intersection and merging as topological operations, and from [Region-growing Iso-surface Extraction](7568-region-growing-iso-surface-extraction.md) by maintaining a distinct boundary front rather than a filled volume.

Unlike [Surface Modeling via Boundary Tracking and Marching Cubes](14379-surface-modeling-via-boundary-tracking-and-marching-cubes.md), which relies on voxel grid topology, this framework operates on general implicit functions without predefined volume components.
**Inputs:** An implicit function $f(\mathbf{x}) = 0$ defining the surface; a seed point $\mathbf{p}_0$ on the surface.
**Outputs:** A manifold triangle mesh approximating the surface.
Each edge is defined by two vertices $(\mathbf{v}_i, \mathbf{v}_j)$.
**Initialization:** Find a seed point $\mathbf{p}_0$ on the surface $f(\mathbf{x})=0$.
**Edge Selection:** Choose an edge $e = (\mathbf{v}_i, \mathbf{v}_j)$ from the current front.
**Triangle Creation:** Compute a new vertex $\mathbf{v}_{new}$ to form a triangle $T = (\mathbf{v}_i, \mathbf{v}_j, \mathbf{v}_{new})$ attached to $e$.
**Self-Intersection Check:** Test if triangle $T$ intersects any existing front edge or triangle.
*   If $T$ causes the front to intersect itself, split the front into two separate fronts at the intersection point.
The new edge created by the split becomes part of the new front boundaries.
**Cross-Front Intersection Check:** Test if $T$ intersects a different, non-adjacent front.
*   If $T$ intersects a different front, merge the two fronts.
The shared boundary edges are removed from the front list, and the new edges formed by the merge are added.
Update the front list by removing edge $e$ and adding the new boundary edges created by $T$.
**Termination:** Repeat steps 2–6 until the front is empty or a coverage criterion is met.
*   **Strengths:** Capable of generating high-quality meshes for general implicit surfaces without predefined volume descriptions.
Handles complex topology through front splitting and merging.
Front intersection detection can be computationally expensive.
Lacks a theoretical foundation for edge size selection in the base framework, relying on heuristics.
*   **When to use:** When extracting meshes from general implicit functions where topological changes (splitting/merging) are expected and high-quality element shapes are required.
Previous works in this area include [8, 23, 24] for implicit surface triangulation and [7, 46] for general mesh generation.
